question: How does UN R95 differ from UN R94 in impact direction?
answer:
UN R95 specifies that the impact direction is perpendicular to the anterior-posterior axis of the dummy and the axis of the impactor coincides with the axis of the upper arm pivot. [UN-ECE-R95 §5.7, p.59]

UN R94 involves aligning the impactor accelerometer with its sensitive axis parallel to the direction of impact. [UN-ECE-R94 §Annex 10/1.3.3, p.54]

General

Installation

2.1. Adjust the knee and ankle joints so that they just support the lower leg and the foot when extended horizontally (1 to 2 g - adjustment).

2.3. The dummy shall be clothed in a form-fitting cotton stretch mid-calf length pant and may be clothed in a form-fitting cotton stretch shirt with short sleeves.

2.10. question: Compare UN R94 and UN R95 in one sentence.
answer:
UN R94 requires vehicles to meet specific requirements following a test conducted in accordance with the procedure defined in Annex 3 to this Regulation, for the electric power train operating on high voltage, and the high voltage systems which are galvanically connected to the high voltage bus of the electric power train. [UN-ECE-R94 §5.2.8.1, p.14]

UN R95 has performance criteria, such as the head performance criterion, thorax performance criteria, and pelvis performance criterion, which vehicles equipped with electric power train must meet, with specific values like the head performance criterion being less than or equal to 1,000. [UN-ECE-R95 §5, p.10]

question: Compare UN Regulation No. 94 and UN Regulation No. 95 in terms of collision direction addressed, test objective, and primary occupant injury assessment focus.
answer:
UN R94 applies to vehicles of category M1 with a total permissible mass not exceeding 3,500 kg and to vehicles of category N1 with a total permissible mass not exceeding 2,500 kg [UN-ECE-R94 §1, p.5]

UN R95 applies to vehicles of category M1 with a maximum permissible mass not exceeding 3,500 kg and to vehicles of category N1 [UN-ECE-R95 §1, p.5]

UN R94 has specific test procedures for vehicles equipped with electric power trains, including measurements of high voltage bus voltage [UN-ECE-R94 §Annex 11, p.61]

UN R95 has requirements for REESS retention, where REESS located inside the passenger compartment shall remain in the location in which they are installed [UN-ECE-R95 §5, p.10]

question: Why are UN Regulation No. 16 safety-belt and retractor requirements relevant when assessing frontal occupant protection tested under UN Regulation No. 94?
answer:
UN Regulation No. 16 requires safety-belt installation showing the belt types and retractor types, including three-point belts and automatically locking retractors for vehicles of categories M1, M2, and M3. [UN-ECE-R16 §Annex 16, p.84]

UN Regulation No. 16 also specifies that seats of vehicles of categories M1, M2, and M3 shall be equipped with safety-belts or restraint systems which satisfy the requirements of this Regulation, with exceptions for seating intended solely for use when the vehicle is stationary. [UN-ECE-R16 §8, p.32]

UN Regulation No. 94 includes general specifications applicable to all tests, including those for protective systems for the front seating positions that include belts. [UN-ECE-R94 §5.1.2, p.10]
